name: Abydosaurus
sum: Abydosaurus is a brachiosaurid sauropod from the Early Cretaceous of Utah, known from complete skulls with narrow teeth.
wsnote: Single estimate by T. Holtz (2012) quoted by the cited Wikipedia revision.
holotype: DINO 16488, a nearly complete skull with lower jaws and the first four neck vertebrae, from the base of the Mussentuchit Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation near Dinosaur National Monument.
material: Skull and neck material; one of the few sauropods known from skulls and the first described complete skull of a Cretaceous sauropod from the Americas.
biology: Its narrow teeth are notable, because earlier brachiosaurids were thought to have broader, spoon-shaped ones.
author: Chure et al. 2010

sources.text: Chure, D.; Britt, B.; Whitlock, J.A.; Wilson, J.A. 2010. First complete sauropod dinosaur skull from the Cretaceous of the Americas and the evolution of sauropod dentition. Naturwissenschaften 97(4): 379–391. doi:10.1007/s00114-010-0650-6
